Examples to start with

        

        
Getting started

        
    
          
  1. Plug the board into the computer with a USB-C cable.
    2. 
          
  2. First time only: click First-time setup and install MicroPython.
    3. 
          
  3. Click Connect board and pick the board from the list.
    4. 
          
  4. Put your blocks under when ▶ clicked (in Events) and click Run. The result shows up on the screen.
    5. 
          
  5. Save to board keeps your program, so it runs every time the board turns on.
    6. 
        

        
The screen

        
0,0171,319

          
Point x=0, y=0 is the top-left corner. x grows to the right up to 171, and y grows downward up to 319.

        
Tips

        
    
          
  • The screen shows English letters, numbers and symbols.
    • 
          
  • The BOOT button on the board also works as a button for your programs.
    • 
          
  • Tilt is measured in degrees, from about -90 to 90.
    • 
          
  • Pins 0, 1 and 10 are on the side headers. They work with 3.3 V only. Never connect 5 V to them, and always put a resistor in front of an LED.
    • 
          
  • The SD card must be formatted as FAT32. Files you write can be opened on a computer.
    • 
          
  • Bluetooth: connect once with the cable, and Bluetooth is put on the board. After that, click Bluetooth and choose the board's name (Screen- and 5 letters) from the list. The board can then run on a battery or a USB charger.
    • 
          
  • If the board stops responding: click Stop. If that doesn't help, press RESET on the board and connect again.
    •

Install MicroPython (first time only)

    
You do this once for each board. It erases whatever was on the board before.

    
    
      
  1. Plug the board into the computer with the USB-C cable. MicroPython v1.29.0 is already inside this app, so there is nothing to download.
    2. 
      
  2. Click Install and pick the board from the list. Wait until the bar is full and it says Done! (about a minute).
    3. 
      
  3. Unplug the cable and plug it back in. Then press the RESET button on the board.
    4. 
      
  4. Close this window and click Connect board. Wait until it says Board connected. The screen library and Bluetooth are already on the board.
    5. 
    

    
If Install doesn't start: unplug the board, hold down BOOT, plug it back in, let go, and click Install again.

    
Another MicroPython version (not needed)
      
Only if you want a different version: choose its .bin file from micropython.org.
